jobs.title: Data Scientist, Marketplace Incentives
jobs.description:
**About Build AI**
------------------


Build AI is the data hyperscaler for Physical AI. We co\-design hardware, collection, infrastructure, and research to scale the in\-the\-wild physical labor dataset by orders of magnitude. We learn from humans doing the real job, in real environments. Inflecting revenue, backed by top\-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Build is becoming the bottleneck to solving physical labor.

**Job Summary**
---------------


This role exists to hillclimb the Head of Dataset \& Quality’s objective. They define the ideal dataset, the objective function, the taxonomy, and the value of incremental data. You take that objective and maximize it: incentives, marketplace design, and collection behavior so the next hour we collect actually moves the score.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Treat the Dataset \& Quality objective / value function as the thing you optimize — not raw hours, not vanity volume
* Design marketplace mechanics (task mix, targeting, bonuses, payouts, eligibility) so collectors produce high\-value data
* Run experiments: treatment assignment, holdouts, pay and bonus tests; keep the ones that hillclimb the objective and kill the rest
* Measure whether incremental collection is improving the dataset under the value function, and report that in language ops can act on
* Work with software to ship incentive and payout changes into the collection product (not a spreadsheet that never lands)
* Watch for Goodhart: collectors optimizing the proxy instead of the objective, and close those holes

**You may be a good fit if you have (Must\-have qualifications)**
-----------------------------------------------------------------

* Quantitative: you can take someone else’s objective function and optimize against it
* Comfortable designing and reading experiments (assignment, holdouts, power, leakage)
* Comfortable with messy field / collection data
* You like iteration: small changes, measured against the objective, shipped again

**Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice\-to\-have qualifications)**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* Experience with marketplaces, incentives, pricing, or growth experimentation (gig, two\-sided, or similar)
* Experience with payouts, bonuses, or pay systems that moved real money
* You have shipped experiment results into a product, not only a notebook

**Benefits**
------------

* Competitive pay
* Medical, dental, and vision packages with generous premium coverage
* $500 per month credit for waiving medical benefits
* Housing subsidy of $2k per month for those living within walking distance of the office
* Relocation support for those moving to San Francisco (Financial District) or Shenzhen (Nanshan)
* Various wellness benefits covering fitness, mental health, and more
* Daily lunch and dinner in our office
* Unlimited compute budget subject to ROI justification
* Travel

**How we're different**
-----------------------


Build believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are betting early on learning from real human work at massive scale, and that the economies of scale of collection beat extra sensors and extra fidelity. Our addressable market is all physical labor, unlike many of our competitors.


We are a fully in\-person team in San Francisco (Financial District) and Shenzhen (Nanshan), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.


Build AI is an equal opportunity employer. We review every application. If you do not meet every bullet, still apply. Questions: research@build.ai


Compensation Range: $180K \- $280K

System engineering work happens across the organization today, but no single person owns it end to end. As platform scope grows and programs multiply, that gap matters more.

jobs.title: AI Context & Data Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
**About Town**
--------------


Town (town.com) is AI that starts from who you are. We build a persistent model of your identity, your voice, your judgment, your relationships, and your priorities, and use it to do real work on your behalf across every tool where you operate: email, calendar, documents, Slack, and more. Town doesn't wait for you to prompt it. It observes, learns, and acts. The more you use it, the more it becomes an extension of you.

  

Town was founded by Jean\-Denis Greze (CEO), former CTO of Plaid, and Tony Vincent (CPO), former Director of Applied AI Product at Google. We're a small, talent\-dense team backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Forerunner Ventures, First Round Capital, and Conviction, with more than $73M raised to date.

**About the role**
------------------


Town is building the most personalized, most capable AI assistant for everyone — and personalization at that level is a retrieval and data problem. The assistant is only as good as the context it can bring into the moment: the right memory, message, document, or relationship, pulled fast and related by meaning across everything a person and their team touch.


You'll build the foundation the whole product reasons over: the search and data infrastructure behind that context. One shared retrieval layer combining lexical and semantic search, the realtime and batch pipelines that keep it fresh and correct, and the durable data model everything else is built on.


This is greenfield and high\-leverage: you'll be the first person building this layer.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Build the search and retrieval layer that puts the right context at every Townie's fingertips, the moment it's needed — one shared layer the whole product pulls from instead of refetching context on its own.
* Combine lexical and semantic search and own the tradeoffs between them: vector vs. lexical, precompute vs. fetch, hybrid retrieval, and ranking.
* Design the durable data model the assistant's work is built on, so context is relevant, fast, and cost\-effective.
* Build and operate the pipelines behind it — realtime/streaming and batch — that keep the index fresh and correct as the underlying data changes.
* Stand up the indexing and storage layer and keep it fast and reliable at scale: latency, cost, freshness, and completeness.
* Lay the groundwork for relating content by meaning across everything the assistant knows — the start of a knowledge graph of people, companies, projects, and how they connect.

**You might thrive here if you...**
-----------------------------------

* Have significant, hands\-on experience across lexical and semantic search components and approaches (BM25, embeddings, ANN/vector indexes, hybrid retrieval, ranking).
* Have run large\-scale data infrastructure, ideally both realtime/streaming and batch — pipelines, indexing, and storage.
* Can make retrieval fast and cheap at scale, and reason about the latency, cost, and freshness tradeoffs cold.
* Are a systems thinker comfortable in greenfield, where the foundation doesn't exist yet.
* Are excited to take these systems from rapid prototype to production scale.
* Bonus if you've worked on ranking/relevance, knowledge graphs, or retrieval for LLM or agentic systems.

  

**Location**
------------


San Francisco, CA. Five days a week in person at our Financial District office.


Compensation Range: $250K \- $300K

We design circuits and boards, own rack integration, and deliver complete hardware systems that extend what user devices can do, host the content people love, and enable the capabilities Apple is bringing to customers now and in the future.  

  

Delivering those experiences requires systems that grow more complex with every program. They span multiple physical racks, high\-speed networking, tiered data storage, energy storage, and custom compute from different teams and vendors. Every piece must work together as one. System engineering work happens across the organization today, but no single person owns it end to end. As platform scope grows and programs multiply, that gap matters more.  

  

The Senior Hardware Systems Engineer closes that gap. This role owns the system: the requirements that define it, the interfaces between its parts, and the documentation that holds it together from the first architecture conversation to handoff to sustaining operations. If that kind of ownership is what you're built for, we want to talk.  

  

**Description**  

  

You will own the system as a whole: the requirements that define it, the interfaces that connect it, the documentation that captures it, and the evidence that proves every part of it works.  

  

You'll work with our architecture team to turn high\-level platform goals into a complete, verifiable set of hardware requirements. Then you'll deliver those requirements to the teams responsible for each piece: custom PCBs, rack enclosures, power delivery and energy storage, networking, data storage, mechanical systems, firmware, and software. You won't build each of those pieces, but you'll know each domain well enough to write requirements they can actually build to, catch problems at boundaries before they become integration surprises, and get every team aligned on what the system needs.  

  

Our platforms integrate custom, semi\-custom, and off\-the\-shelf hardware across multiple programs running in parallel. Requirements take shape during the architecture and high\-level design process, and one of the most important things this role does is pull that work as early as possible. A requirement discovered during detailed design is expensive, and one discovered during validation testing is far more disruptive. Your job is to lead the requirements process at the system level from the very start: make decisions, document them with enough rigor that a sustaining team can depend on them years from now, and keep the whole picture in focus while everyone else is heads\-down in their domain.  

  

The right person for this role has done it before, though not necessarily in a datacenter. We'd rather hire someone who has already lived through a fundamental shift in what a system needs to be. Fields like defense, aerospace, automotive, and industrial systems have been solving exactly this class of problem for decades. What we need is someone who can write a requirement that can be tested, own a room full of specialists and drive them to agreement, and see three moves ahead when a change in one sub\-system creates a problem somewhere else. **You’ll be joining Adobe on a contract opportunity, employed through NextDeavor**

**Benefits You'll Love**

NextDeavor offers health, vision and dental benefits for contract employees Paid sick leave eligibility is contingent on state of residence Optional 401k Plan (excludes employer match) Opportunity to get your foot in the door at a well\-established corporation, with potential for extended or permanent full\-time employment

**Become a Key Player as a a Data Engineer 1**

You will design and maintain scalable data solutions that enable the client's growth monetization efforts and drive measurable product and marketing outcomes. You will partner closely with Data Science, Product, Marketing, and Engineering stakeholders to deliver reliable pipelines and actionable insights. This role supports an 8\-hour shift with a guaranteed 40 hours per week.

**Here's How You'll Make an Impact on the Team**

* Design, build, optimize, and maintain scalable data pipelines to support growth monetization initiatives
* Write and optimize complex SQL queries to analyze A/B experiment results
* Develop and enhance ETL/ELT workflows for large\-scale structured and unstructured datasets
* Optimize pipeline performance, reliability, scalability, and data quality across distributed systems
* Work with Big Data technologies and best practices to process high\-volume datasets efficiently
* Build automated monitoring, alerting, and validation frameworks for pipeline health and data integrity
* Partner with Data Science, Product, Marketing, and Engineering teams to deliver actionable insights and scalable data solutions

**Here's What You'll Need to Be Successful in This Role**

* Strong SQL expertise with the ability to write and optimize complex queries on large datasets
* Hands\-on experience with Big Data technologies such as Hadoop, Hive, Spark, or similar distributed processing frameworks
* Experience building and optimizing scalable data pipelines in cloud and enterprise environments
* Proficiency in ETL orchestration and workflow management tools
* Experience with data quality, pipeline monitoring, and performance tuning
* Ability to collaborate effectively with technical and non\-technical stakeholders in a fast\-paced environment
* Minimum 5 years of experience required

$55\.21 \- $69\.01/hour
